[PERSISTENT EXPERIENCE GUIDANCE]
## Consolidated Experience from Similar Tasks
Manipulation tasks are only successful when their preconditions are explicitly satisfied. Before any pick-up, the robot must navigate to the target object and verify it is nearby and reachable; attempting to pick up an object that is not near the robot fails. Before any place action, the robot must verify that it is actually holding the target object; otherwise the place action will not move anything. More generally, do not assume that a skill will succeed just because it was invoked—first confirm proximity/location for pick-up and held-object state for placement, then verify the result after execution.

## Preliminary Thinking
1. Locate the Rubik's cube on the left counter. 2. Navigate to the cube and confirm it is within reach. 3. Execute the pick-up action for the cube. 4. Verify that the robot is holding the cube. If not, reattempt after confirming proximity. 5. Navigate to the right receptacle of the left counter. 6. Confirm the robot is at the correct target location and still holding the cube. 7. Execute the place action into the right receptacle. 8. Verify that the cube has been placed in the right receptacle and is no longer held.
[/PERSISTENT EXPERIENCE GUIDANCE]
